title: Joshua 2: Rahab and the Spies
body:
Read the chapter → [Joshua 2](/bible/joshua/2)

**[Joshua 2:1-7](/bible/joshua/2#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/joshua/2#v1)</sup> And Joshua the son of Nun sent out of Shittim two men to spy secretly, saying, Go view the land, even Jericho. And they went, and came into an harlot’s house, named Rahab, and lodged there.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/joshua/2#v2)</sup> And it was told the king of Jericho, saying, Behold, there came men in hither to night of the children of Israel to search out the country.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/joshua/2#v3)</sup> And the king of Jericho sent unto Rahab, saying, Bring forth the men that are come to thee, which are entered into thine house: for they be come to search out all the country.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/joshua/2#v4)</sup> And the woman took the two men, and hid them, and said thus, There came men unto me, but I wist not whence they were:
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/joshua/2#v5)</sup> And it came to pass about the time of shutting of the gate, when it was dark, that the men went out: whither the men went I wot not: pursue after them quickly; for ye shall overtake them.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/joshua/2#v6)</sup> But she had brought them up to the roof of the house, and hid them with the stalks of flax, which she had laid in order upon the roof.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/joshua/2#v7)</sup> And the men pursued after them the way to Jordan unto the fords: and as soon as they which pursued after them were gone out, they shut the gate.

- Joshua sent two men out of Shittim to spy secretly and view the land, even Jericho, and they came into the house of a harlot named Rahab and lodged there.
- Word made its way to the king of Jericho that men of the children of Israel had come to search out the country, and he sent unto Rahab to bring them forth. She had taken the two men and hid them on the roof under the stalks of flax she had laid in order there.
- She told the king's men the truth in part and misdirection in the rest: men came unto me, but I wist not whence they were, and they went out about the time of the shutting of the gate; pursue after them quickly. The pursuers chased toward Jordan after men who had gone nowhere, the gate was shut behind them, and the spies had clearance to escape. A heathen woman looked out for Israel, and she did it out of the fear of the Lord, as her own words show.

**[Joshua 2:8-11](/bible/joshua/2#v8)**

> <sup>[8](/bible/joshua/2#v8)</sup> And before they were laid down, she came up unto them upon the roof;
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/joshua/2#v9)</sup> And she said unto the men, I know that the Lord hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/joshua/2#v10)</sup> For we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red sea for you, when ye came out of Egypt; and what ye did unto the two kings of the Amorites, that were on the other side Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom ye utterly destroyed.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/joshua/2#v11)</sup> And as soon as we had heard these things, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man, because of you: for the Lord your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath.

- Before the spies lay down, Rahab came up to the roof and confessed: I know that the Lord hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you. That is faith and belief; a heathen acknowledged that the God of Israel had ordained them to conquer her land.

  Precepts:
  - **[Matthew 15:27-28](/bible/matthew/15#v27)**
    > <sup>[27](/bible/matthew/15#v27)</sup> And she said, Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.
    >
    > <sup>[28](/bible/matthew/15#v28)</sup> Then Jesus answered and said unto her, O woman, great is thy faith: be it unto thee even as thou wilt. And her daughter was made whole from that very hour.

    Like the woman who answered, Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters' table, and Christ said, great is thy faith; Rahab is a heathen whose faith the Lord honoured.

- Her faith came by report: we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red Sea for you, and what ye did unto Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites whom ye utterly destroyed; and as soon as we had heard it, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man. The Lord had said he would put that spirit on the nations.

  Precepts:
  - **[Numbers 21:34-35](/bible/numbers/21#v34)**
    > <sup>[34](/bible/numbers/21#v34)</sup> And the Lord said unto Moses, Fear him not: for I have delivered him into thy hand, and all his people, and his land; and thou shalt do to him as thou didst unto Sihon king of the Amorites, which dwelt at Heshbon.
    >
    > <sup>[35](/bible/numbers/21#v35)</sup> So they smote him, and his sons, and all his people, until there was none left him alive: and they possessed his land.

    The destruction of Sihon and Og on the other side Jordan was the report that reached Jericho.
  - **[Deuteronomy 2:25](/bible/deuteronomy/2#v25)**
    > <sup>[25](/bible/deuteronomy/2#v25)</sup> This day will I begin to put the dread of thee and the fear of thee upon the nations that are under the whole heaven, who shall hear report of thee, and shall tremble, and be in anguish because of thee.

    This day will I begin to put the dread of thee and the fear of thee upon the nations, who shall hear report of thee, and shall tremble and be in anguish because of thee; Rahab's melted heart is that word fulfilled.

- Faith and fear go hand in hand. Rahab knew the Lord is not to be played with when it comes to this people, and that fear is what gave her the faith to put her life on the line. She might get caught by her king for hiding the spies, but what she really feared was the judgment of their God if she did not help them.

  Precepts:
  - **[Hebrews 11:31](/bible/hebrews/11#v31)**
    > <sup>[31](/bible/hebrews/11#v31)</sup> By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace.

    By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace; her fear of the Lord worked faith, and that faith saved her.

**[Joshua 2:12-21](/bible/joshua/2#v12)**

> <sup>[12](/bible/joshua/2#v12)</sup> Now therefore, I pray you, swear unto me by the Lord, since I have shewed you kindness, that ye will also shew kindness unto my father’s house, and give me a true token:
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/joshua/2#v13)</sup> And that ye will save alive my father, and my mother, and my brethren, and my sisters, and all that they have, and deliver our lives from death.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/joshua/2#v14)</sup> And the men answered her, Our life for yours, if ye utter not this our business. And it shall be, when the Lord hath given us the land, that we will deal kindly and truly with thee.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/joshua/2#v15)</sup> Then she let them down by a cord through the window: for her house was upon the town wall, and she dwelt upon the wall.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/joshua/2#v16)</sup> And she said unto them, Get you to the mountain, lest the pursuers meet you; and hide yourselves there three days, until the pursuers be returned: and afterward may ye go your way.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/joshua/2#v17)</sup> And the men said unto her, We will be blameless of this thine oath which thou hast made us swear.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/joshua/2#v18)</sup> Behold, when we come into the land, thou shalt bind this line of scarlet thread in the window which thou didst let us down by: and thou shalt bring thy father, and thy mother, and thy brethren, and all thy father’s household, home unto thee.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/joshua/2#v19)</sup> And it shall be, that whosoever shall go out of the doors of thy house into the street, his blood shall be upon his head, and we will be guiltless: and whosoever shall be with thee in the house, his blood shall be on our head, if any hand be upon him.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/joshua/2#v20)</sup> And if thou utter this our business, then we will be quit of thine oath which thou hast made us to swear.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/joshua/2#v21)</sup> And she said, According unto your words, so be it. And she sent them away, and they departed: and she bound the scarlet line in the window.

- Rahab asked the spies to swear unto her by the Lord, since she had shewed them kindness, that they would shew kindness unto her father's house and give her a true token, saving her father, mother, brethren, and sisters alive.
- The men answered, our life for yours, if ye utter not this our business: since she looked out for Israel, Israel would look out for her, on condition the plan stayed secret. If she uttered the business, the oath was null and void.
- The token was the line of scarlet thread bound in the window by which she let them down, for her house was upon the town wall. That scarlet line marked her house so no one in it would be slain when Israel came into the land; the terms were that whosoever went out of the doors into the street, his blood would be on his own head, and whosoever stayed within, his blood on Israel's head if any hand touched him.
- She sent them to the mountain to hide three days until the pursuers returned, said according unto your words, so be it, and bound the scarlet line in the window.

**[Joshua 2:22-24](/bible/joshua/2#v22)**

> <sup>[22](/bible/joshua/2#v22)</sup> And they went, and came unto the mountain, and abode there three days, until the pursuers were returned: and the pursuers sought them throughout all the way, but found them not.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/joshua/2#v23)</sup> So the two men returned, and descended from the mountain, and passed over, and came to Joshua the son of Nun, and told him all things that befell them:
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/joshua/2#v24)</sup> And they said unto Joshua, Truly the Lord hath delivered into our hands all the land; for even all the inhabitants of the country do faint because of us.

- The spies abode in the mountain three days until the pursuers returned, having sought them throughout all the way and found them not.
- They came again to Joshua and reported: truly the Lord hath delivered into our hands all the land, for even all the inhabitants of the country do faint because of us. The land was theirs for the taking, exactly as the Lord had promised.
